# Results — Study 847 (Rotten-Tomatoes -> Studio)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
**a big film's critic reception (a coarse Rotten-Tomatoes tier: fresh vs. rotten) moves
its distributing studio's stock around the release.** Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped) — a clean run is
stamped as-of 2026-06-30 with no partial month. Fingerprint `567671346662` (the SPY +
six-studio close panel). Per-ticker fingerprints: `d57404af997d`
SPY / `1f215beecb34` DIS / `ec1bfa8df210` WBD / `1c6e31d1e522` PARA / `88dadf4247a2` CMCSA
/ `a538858b0952` NFLX / `ba00ad7266b7` SONY.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily total-return closes for **SPY + DIS / WBD / PARA / CMCSA / NFLX / SONY** (1,276 rows each, 2021-06-01 → 2026-06-30) |
| Film table | **hardcoded** table of **40 major wide releases** 2022-04-01 → 2025-06-20, each with (title, distributing-studio ticker, real opening/premiere date, coarse critic tier, approx. Tomatometer). Only **clearly fresh (≥ 75)** or **clearly rotten (< 50)** titles — mixed 50-74 excluded so the contrast is unambiguous. **21 fresh / 19 rotten.** Sources: Rotten Tomatoes (Tomatometer), Box Office Mojo (opening date + distributor), trade press |
| Analysis input | the **tier bucket only** (fresh/rotten); the stored score is reference-only |
| Statistics | one-sample *t* per tier + a **Welch *t*** on the fresh-minus-rotten gap (the quantity the claim predicts to be positive); Wilson intervals on hit rates; a **20-seed × 1,000-draw tier-label permutation** placebo on the gap; a **20-seed × 200-draw random-date** placebo on the pooled magnitude; Newey-West cross-check |
| Windows | two pre-registered event windows on the studio's market-adjusted abnormal return, anchored at the first NYSE session on/after release: **opening-weekend `[0..+1]`** and **following-week `[+2..+6]`** |
| Execution / costs | one documented convention: the release date is snapped to the first NYSE session on/after it (the study's single execution lag). The timer is long-fresh / short-rotten on the following-week window: one round trip = 2 × one-way cost × NAV per leg, plus annual borrow on the short (rotten) legs |
| Survivorship / coverage (named) | **WBD** trades only from 2022-04-11 (WarnerMedia-Discovery merger), **PARA** is the post-2022-02 Paramount Global re-brand — the table's WBD/PARA titles are all dated after those tickers existed. **NFLX** has no theatrical opening weekend: its event is the **streaming-premiere** date (named honestly; a different event type pooled with the theatrical majors). All 40 films resolve to a full window on the real tape |

**Abnormal return** = studio daily return − SPY daily return (a beta = 1 market model),
then demeaned by the series' own 2022-2026 mean (a constant-mean overlay), so a nonzero
event-window CAR is not just "this studio drifted that year". **Studio ≠ film label:**
each is a conglomerate (parks, ISPs, streaming, TV, games) for which one film is a tiny
revenue sliver — the efficient-markets prior is a null.

## The clean, direct window — opening-weekend CAR `[0..+1]`

This is the window where a pre-released critic verdict (review embargoes lift days before
a wide release) should first hit the stock.

| tier | n | mean opening-weekend CAR | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| fresh | 21 | **−110.6 bps** | −1.65 |
| rotten | 19 | **−98.8 bps** | −1.45 |
| **fresh − rotten gap** | | **−11.9 bps** | **Welch *t* = −0.12** |

**Nothing.** On the release-weekend window the two tiers move together (both mildly
negative, a mechanical "sell the release" wobble common to *all* big releases), and the
fresh-minus-rotten gap is **−11.9 bps at *t* = −0.12** — indistinguishable from zero, and
if anything the wrong sign. On the window where a review effect should be sharpest, there
is no tier signal at all.

## The following-week window `[+2..+6]` — where a gap *does* appear

| tier | n | mean following-week CAR | one-sample *t* | Newey-West *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| fresh | 21 | **+181.1 bps** | +1.62 | +2.51 |
| rotten | 19 | **−634.6 bps** | −2.14 | −2.09 |
| **fresh − rotten gap** | | **+815.7 bps** | **Welch *t* = +2.58** | |

Combined window `[0..+6]`: fresh +70.5 bps (*t* = +0.67), rotten −733.3 bps (*t* = −2.18),
gap **+803.8 bps** (Welch *t* = +2.28).

Following-week hit rates: fresh studio **up 17/21 = 81.0%** (Wilson [60.0%, 92.3%]); rotten
studio **down 14/19 = 73.7%** (Wilson [51.2%, 88.2%]).

Here a **right-signed, statistically significant** gap shows up: rotten-scored releases'
studios drift down ~6.3% (market-adjusted) over the following trading week while
fresh-scored ones drift up ~1.8%. **Tier-label permutation placebo:** observed gap
+815.7 bps vs a null of +0.6 bps (sd 328.3) over **20,000 draws → right-tail p = 0.001**.
Taken alone, this clears the desk's |*t*| ≥ 2 bar with the sign the claim predicts.

## Why this is stamped **Weak**, not Real — the credibility checks it fails

A significant, right-signed, sub-era-robust gap is exactly the moment to get *more*
skeptical, not less. Four checks say this is not a believable causal review effect:

1. **No reaction in the direct window.** The opening-weekend `[0..+1]` gap is **−11.9 bps,
   *t* = −0.12** — dead flat. Reviews are public *before* release; a genuine "reviews move
   the studio" effect should be sharpest immediately, not appear only on days +2..+6.
2. **The effect is a single transient window that then reverses.** Fresh-minus-rotten gap
   by window: pre-release `[−6..−2]` **−210 bps** (*t* = −1.26), `[−11..−2]` **−26 bps**
   (*t* = −0.11), opening `[0..+1]` **−12 bps** (*t* = −0.12), following-week `[+2..+6]`
   **+816 bps** (*t* = +2.58), `[+7..+11]` **+79 bps** (*t* = +0.33), `[+15..+20]`
   **−106 bps** (*t* = −0.70). One window lights up; the rest — including the two windows
   *before* the release — are flat, and the effect has decayed to noise by `[+7..+11]`.
3. **The pooled magnitude is not unusual.** The random-date placebo on the *pooled*
   following-week CAR (−206.3 bps) gives **two-sided p = 0.079** over 4,000 draws — a
   release week is *not* a bigger-than-random move for these studios. Only the *split by
   tier* is significant, which is what a **confound correlated with tier** produces.
4. **Economic implausibility + a known confound.** A ~5-8% weekly *abnormal* move on a
   ~$100-200bn conglomerate from one film is not credible. The two largest "rotten drops"
   are Paramount's *IF* (−44%) and *Bob Marley: One Love* (−40%) — those are **PARA's
   spring-2024 Skydance-takeover crashes**, not the films. More broadly, structurally
   declining studios (WBD, PARA) both greenlight worse-reviewed films *and* carry weaker
   stocks in the same period: the tier is a **proxy for the studio's contemporaneous
   fortunes**, not a lever on the price. (Trimming the three |CAR| > 15% outliers does
   *not* kill the split — it strengthens it to Welch *t* = +4.59 — precisely because the
   gap is a broad ambient tilt across many events, not two outliers: consistent with
   selection, not with a clean single-film information shock.)

**Robustness (for completeness, not rehabilitation):** the split holds in both sub-eras
(2022-2023 gap +365 bps, *t* = +2.03; 2024-2025 +1,352 bps, *t* = +2.18) and every
leave-one-studio-out (Welch *t* between +2.16 and +2.84). It is a *real in-sample
association* — that is why the stamp is **Weak, not None** — but it is not attributable to
the film's reception, so it is **not Real.**

## The timer — long-fresh / short-rotten the studio over the following week

| cost (one-way / leg) | gross | net | *t* (net) | n legs |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps | +396.5 bps | +396.2 bps | +2.56 | 40 |
| 5.0 bps (+ 50 bps/yr borrow) | +396.5 bps | +386.2 bps | +2.50 | 40 |

The naive costed book **survives** (net +386 bps/leg, *t* = +2.50) — but it rides
entirely on the same 40-event, single-window, look-elsewhere gap: it presumes you knew
ex ante that `[+2..+6]` (and not `[0..+1]`, nor `[+7..+11]`) was the window that would
work, its per-leg magnitude is inflated by studio-idiosyncratic news (the Paramount
crashes), and it is a 40-trade sample with a right-signed but non-causal driver. That is a
**Fragile**, not investable, result: it is a backtest artifact of a Weak signal, not a
deployable edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic paired (studio, benchmark) log-return world with a TUNABLE planted tier
drift on the following-week window; no network.

| world | fresh-minus-rotten gap Welch *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.12** (sd 0.95), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = 0.004/day, **20 seeds** | mean **+4.49** (sd 1.20), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 20/20 seeds** |
| planted edge = 0.004/day (seed 847) | gap +349 bps, *t* = **+2.78** |

The detector never fires on the null and lights up sharply on a planted tier effect — the
machinery is faithful and unbiased. *(A power/faithfulness check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp; note the detector's realistic power at n≈20/tier is
modest, another reason to treat a lone real-tape t = 2.58 with caution.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The opening-weekend window — where a pre-released critic verdict
  should first land — shows **no tier gap** (−11.9 bps, Welch *t* = −0.12). A
  right-signed, significant gap appears only in the following-week window (+815.7 bps,
  Welch *t* = +2.58, permutation p = 0.001, robust to sub-era and leave-one-studio-out),
  but it fails every credibility check: no direct-window reaction, a single transient
  window that reverses afterward, a pooled magnitude indistinguishable from random weeks
  (p = 0.079), and an economically implausible size driven by studio-idiosyncratic news
  (Paramount's takeover crashes) and by the fact that struggling studios make both worse
  films and worse stocks. A genuine in-sample association that is **not attributable to
  critic reception** — hence Weak, not Real, and not None.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** A long-fresh / short-rotten studio book survives naive costs
  in-sample (net +386 bps/leg, *t* = +2.50, borrow-feasible on large caps), but it is a
  40-trade backtest of a window-selected, non-causal gap — an artifact of the Weak
  signal, not a deployable edge.
- **"Does a flop tank the studio?" — OVERSTATED.** In this 2022-2025 sample a rotten
  score does *line up* with a soft following week — but there is zero opening-weekend
  reaction, the move is a single transient window, its magnitude is implausible for a
  conglomerate, and it is inseparable from the studios' ambient fortunes. The folklore's
  causal story ("the flop tanked the stock") is not supported; a much smaller, harder-to-
  attribute correlation is all that survives, at this study's power (n = 40 events).
